key_insight: The study shows that biomedical AI explanations can be turned into machine-checkable evidence claims, separating verifiability from prediction quality.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinical teams audit whether AI-generated radiogenomic statements are actually supported by the patient-specific imaging evidence before they are used in decisions.
method: Aligned UPenn-GBM radiomics with independent CaPTk-extracted MRI features and expert-validated segmentations.
Built a semantic evidence ledger from 1,728 features across T1, T1GD, T2, and FLAIR in three tumor regions.
Tested deterministic claim verification, corruption robustness, and an LLM-based claim-extraction pilot.
evidence_signal: Across 611 reference cases and an external cohort, semantic-state agreement was moderate-to-strong overall (median 0.786; weighted kappa 0.709), and the verifier reached 100% accuracy in a 6,620-claim corruption benchmark.
watch_item: The framework verifies consistency of claims, but real-world use still depends on standardized imaging, reliable segmentation, and careful handling of features with weaker cross-cohort transportability.
paper_title: Evidence-Bound Reasoning: Neuro-Semantic Verification of Biomedical AI in Glioblastoma Radiogenomics
